title: Derived base change for ring cotangent complexes
statement: Let $A\to C$, $A\to A'$, $C\to C'$ and $A'\to C'$ be a commutative square of homomorphisms of commutative rings. Write $D(T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(T))$ for the derived category of ordinary $T$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and compute derived tensor products using flat resolutions. Assume that the canonical multiplication map $\mu:C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to C'[0]$ induced by this square is a quasi-isomorphism in $D(A')$. For the standard cotangent complexes and their square-induced functoriality maps [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], the canonical $C'$-linear base-change morphism $\beta:L_{C/A}\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}C'\longrightarrow L_{C'/A'}$ is an isomorphism in $D(C')$. Here $\beta$ is the derived extension-of-scalars adjoint of the functoriality morphism $L_{C/A}\to L_{C'/A'}$, where the target of the latter is viewed as a complex of $C$-modules via $C\to C'$.

source.place: Tag 08QQ (lemma-flat-base-change-cotangent-complex), with the commutative square equation-commutative-square and its functoriality map in section-functoriality. The hypothesis is the canonical derived-tensor quasi-isomorphism, as applied in Tag 08SJ (lemma-mod-regular-sequence).

proof.text: Take the standard polynomial resolution $P_\bullet\to C$ of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], and write $S=s(P_\bullet)$, $q:S\to C[0]$. It is a quasi-isomorphism and $S^{-n}=P_n$, with no positive terms. Choose polynomial coordinates $P_n=A[x_i\mid i\in I_n]$. By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], its monomials form an $A$-module basis. Tensoring a free module with a module $M$ identifies it with finitely supported families in $M$: the mutually inverse maps send $x^\alpha\otimes m$ to the family with entry $m$ at $\alpha$, and a family $(m_\alpha)$ to $\sum_\alpha x^\alpha\otimes m_\alpha$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Exactness is coordinatewise, and a preimage needs only the finitely many nonzero coordinates. Thus the $P_n$ are flat. The ordinary-module bounded-above flat criterion [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $S$ K-flat, so $q$ is a K-flat resolution of $C[0]$.

source.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), free resolution s(P); more-algebra.tex Tag 064K (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism).

proof.text: Use the exact tensor equivalence of [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification] to interpret [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and the normalized adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] in ordinary modules. For $A\to A'$, computation on the K-flat resolution $q$ identifies $C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$ with $S\otimes_A A'$. The canonical map $\mu$ is represented by $\epsilon'(p\otimes a')=f(\epsilon(p))a'$ in degree zero and zero in negative degrees, where $f:C\to C'$ is the given map: this is exactly the adjunct formula $x\otimes a'\mapsto a'g(x)$ applied to $g=fq$. Consequently $\epsilon'$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the hypothesis. Its degree-zero cohomology is the canonical ring homomorphism $\alpha:C\otimes_A A'\to C'$, $c\otimes a'\mapsto f(c)a'$. Indeed $H^0(S\otimes_A A')=\operatorname{coker}(d_S^{-1}\otimes1)=C\otimes_A A'$: a bilinear map from $S^0\times A'$ kills $\operatorname{im}d_S^{-1}$ exactly when it factors through $C\times A'$, which proves this cokernel identity from [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus $\alpha$ is bijective, hence an isomorphism of rings; its multiplicativity follows directly from the displayed formula. No flatness of either ring map has been inferred.

source.place: Tag 08QQ hypothesis and Tag 08QP resolution computation; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), normalized by derived.tex Tags 0FND/09T5.

proof.text: Put $D=C\otimes_A A'$ with its algebra base-change structure [def-weil-module-base-change]. The canonical derived-to-ordinary map $C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to D[0]$ is $\alpha^{-1}\mu$: on the resolution of Step 2, both send $p\otimes a'$ to $\epsilon(p)\otimes a'$. It is therefore a quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-tor-independent-cotangent-base-change] to $P_\bullet\to C$ and this map. It says that $P'_\bullet=P_\bullet\otimes_A A'\to D$ is a polynomial resolution with its tensor augmentation. Composing that augmentation with the ring isomorphism $\alpha$ gives a polynomial resolution of $C'$: termwise surjectivity and the augmentation quasi-isomorphism are preserved by an isomorphism. Its augmentation is precisely $p\otimes a'\mapsto f(\epsilon(p))a'$. This verifies every condition of the polynomial-resolution convention in [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence].

source.place: Tags 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), 08QI (remark-resolution); identification of the canonical tensor augmentation.

proof.text: Let $K=s(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}C)$, which is the standard representative of $L_{C/A}$ by [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. The arbitrary-variable basis theorem [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables], applied to each $P_n$, identifies $K^{-n}$ with $\bigoplus_{i\in I_n}C\,\mathrm dx_i$. This includes infinite or empty $I_n$. These modules are flat: after tensoring with $M$ they are finitely supported families in $M$, so an exact sequence remains exact by lifting each of its finitely many nonzero coordinates [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Since $K^{j}=0$ for $j>0$, [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $K$ K-flat.

source.place: Tag 08QQ, flatness of polynomial differentials; algebra.tex Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring); more-algebra.tex Tag 064K.

proof.text:
Write $K'=s(\Omega^1_{P'_\bullet/A'}\otimes_{P'_\bullet}C')$. For each $n$ define
$$\theta_n:(\Omega^1_{P_n/A}\otimes_{P_n}C)\otimes_C C'\longrightarrow\Omega^1_{P'_n/A'}\otimes_{P'_n}C',\qquad (\mathrm dp\otimes c)\otimes b'\longmapsto\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes f(c)b'.$$
The universal derivation [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] makes this map well defined: the right-hand rule is additive, obeys Leibniz in $p$, vanishes on $A$, and is balanced for both scalar extensions [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Coefficient and variable evaluation identify $P_n\otimes_A A'$ with $A'[x_i\mid i\in I_n]$; inverse maps fix $A'$ and send $x_i$ to $x_i\otimes1$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables], both sides of $\theta_n$ are free $C'$-modules on the same $I_n$, and $\theta_n$ sends $(\mathrm dx_i\otimes1)\otimes1$ to $\mathrm d(x_i\otimes1)\otimes1$. The inverse sends this latter basis vector back to the former, so $\theta_n$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08QQ, identification of polynomial differential modules after base change; algebra.tex Tag 00RX.

proof.text: For every face or degeneracy $v:P_n\to P_m$, its scalar extension sends $p\otimes1$ to $v(p)\otimes1$. Following either route through $\theta_n,\theta_m$ therefore sends $(\mathrm dp\otimes c)\otimes b'$ to $\mathrm d(v(p)\otimes1)\otimes f(c)b'$. These elements generate the source, by the universal differential and tensor presentations [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus $\theta$ commutes with every simplicial operator, hence with the alternating sums defining the differentials in [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Taking the alternating complexes gives a chain isomorphism $\theta:K\otimes_C C'\xrightarrow{\sim}K'$, with no normalization or infinite totalization interchange.

source.place: Tag 08QQ, the differential-module identification; section-functoriality (Tag 08QL), associated-complex convention of Tag 08QI.

proof.text: Let $R_\bullet=P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(C'/A')$. The original ring square induces $t:P_\bullet\to R_\bullet$ by [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Its scalar extension $h:P'_\bullet\to R_\bullet$ is $h(p\otimes a')=t(p)a'$. Balancing follows from semilinearity of $t$; each face, degeneracy and augmentation commutes because it commutes with $t$ and fixes $A'$. Both $P'$ (Step 3) and $R$ are polynomial resolutions of $C'$. The comparison clause of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] gives isomorphisms $c_{P'}:K'\simeq L_{C'/A'}$ and $c_R:K(R)\simeq L_{C'/A'}$, with $c_RK(h)=c_{P'}$. In particular $K(h)$ is an isomorphism in $D(C')$. Its map on differentials sends $\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes b'$ to $\mathrm d(t(p))\otimes b'$. The final functoriality clause of that same node therefore identifies the specified map $L_{C/A}\to\operatorname{Res}_fL_{C'/A'}$ with $c_R\circ Q(K(h))\circ Q(\theta)\circ Q(u)$, where $u:K\to\operatorname{Res}_f(K\otimes_C C')$ is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. On generators both sides are $\mathrm dp\otimes c\mapsto\mathrm d(t(p))\otimes f(c)$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), explicit standard resolution map; Tag 08QI (remark-resolution), natural comparisons.

proof.text:
For $f:C\to C'$, the ordinary-module counit theorem [lem-pc-kflat-scalar-extension-counit], applied to the K-flat $K$ of Step 4, gives the computation isomorphism $c_K:L_{C/A}\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}C'\simeq Q(K\otimes_C C')$. Use [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification] to transport the normalized unit and adjunct formulas of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] to ordinary modules. The derived unit at $QK$ is $Q(u)$ under $c_K$, and the adjunct of the generator map in Step 7 is consequently
$$c_R\circ Q(K(h))\circ Q(\theta)\circ c_K.$$
Indeed its adjunction transpose is the Step 7 composite, since $u(x)=x\otimes1$; naturality in the target allows the final factor $c_R$. By the definition in the statement this adjunct is exactly $\beta$. Each factor is an isomorphism: $c_K$ by K-flat computation, $Q(\theta)$ by Step 6, and $c_RQ(K(h))=c_{P'}$ by Step 7. Hence the canonical $\beta$ is an isomorphism in $D(C')$.
